Techniques for separating space complexity classes

sources.title: Nondeterministic Space is Closed under Complementation
sources.locator: SIAM J. Comput. 17(5), pp. 935–938; main theorem
sources.notes: Independently proved by Szelepcsényi.

sources.title: Two Applications of Inductive Counting for Complementation Problems
sources.locator: §3.1; LOGCFL = uniform SAC¹ and complement closure
sources.notes: Authors Borodin, Cook, Dymond, Ruzzo, Tompa; DOI 10.1137/0218038. Contains NL ⊆ SAC¹ ⊆ AC¹ ⊆ NC².

sources.title: Computational Complexity of Probabilistic Turing Machines
sources.locator: SIAM J. Comput. 6(4), pp. 675–695; probabilistic class definitions
sources.notes: Binary fair coins, bounded error on every input.

sources.title: Two theorems on random polynomial time
sources.notes: Original theorem covers RP; BPP extension is attributed to Bennett–Gill. DOI 10.1109/SFCS.1978.37.

sources.title: Relative to a Random Oracle A, P^A ≠ NP^A ≠ co-NP^A with Probability 1
sources.notes: Used only for BPP ⊆ P/poly; oracle separations are not unrelativized separations.

sources.title: BPP and the polynomial hierarchy
sources.locator: Information Processing Letters 17(4), pp. 215–217; main theorem
sources.notes: BPP ⊆ Σ₂P; complement closure gives Π₂P.

sources.title: The polynomial-time hierarchy
sources.notes: DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(76)90061-X; hierarchy and collapse framework.

sources.title: Some connections between nonuniform and uniform complexity classes
sources.notes: The Σ₂P version includes Sipser’s improvement; see AB2007 Theorem 6.13.

sources.title: PP is as Hard as the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy
sources.locator: SIAM J. Comput. 20(5), pp. 865–877; PH ⊆ P^PP
sources.notes: Does not assert PH ⊆ PP.

sources.title: BPP Has Subexponential Time Simulations unless EXPTIME has Publishable Proofs
sources.notes: Conference version 1991; journal Computational Complexity 3, pp. 307–318. EXP ⊆ P/poly ⇒ EXP = MA.

sources.title: P = BPP if E requires exponential circuits: derandomizing the XOR lemma
sources.notes: Exponential circuit hardness; mere E ⊄ P/poly is insufficient for this implication.

sources.title: Nonuniform ACC Circuit Lower Bounds
sources.notes: DOI 10.1145/2559903. Theorem 1.1 gives NTIME[2^n] ⊄ ACC0. Ignore stale journal-template footer dates.

sources.title: Parity, Circuits, and the Polynomial-Time Hierarchy
sources.locator: Main parity lower bound; Mathematical Systems Theory 17, pp. 13–27
sources.notes: Parity is in both L and ACC0 but not nonuniform AC0.

sources.title: IP = PSPACE
sources.locator: JACM 39(4), pp. 869–877; honest prover uses polynomial space
sources.notes: Supports PSPACE ⊆ P/poly ⇒ PSPACE = MA by hardwiring the prover.

sources.title: P = ? NP
sources.notes: Author survey with proofs of padding and PSPACE circuit-collapse consequences; not an exhaustive 2026 audit.

sources.title: Elementary derivations recorded for this benchmark
sources.locator: Unary witness, padding, hardwiring, and intersection arguments
sources.notes: Benchmark-specific proof commentary attached to standard counting, padding and simulation arguments. Recording date is not a publication date or independent evidence of historical novelty.

sources.title: On Relating Time and Space to Size and Depth
sources.locator: SIAM J. Comput. 6(4), pp. 733–744; circuit-depth/space simulation
sources.notes: DOI 10.1137/0206054. Uniform NC uses polylogarithmic space.

sources.title: Trading group theory for randomness
sources.locator: STOC pp. 421–429; AM hierarchy and AM ⊆ Π₂P
sources.notes: AM containment also stated explicitly in AGH1990 §1.1.

sources.title: On the Power of Interaction
sources.notes: Authors Aiello, Goldwasser, Håstad; Combinatorica 10, pp. 3–25.

sources.title: In Search of an Easy Witness: Exponential Time vs. Probabilistic Polynomial Time
sources.notes: Author manuscript. The paper explicitly notes this unconditional containment; amplification and fixing random coins is the elementary proof.

sources.title: On the Power of Probabilistic Polynomial Time: P^NP[log] ⊆ PP
sources.locator: University of Rochester technical report TR275, February 1989, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.3
sources.notes: Beigel, Hemachandra, and Wechsung. Original report date is February 1989; later repository deposit dates do not date the theorem.

sources.title: A Simple Proof of Toda’s Theorem
sources.locator: Theory of Computing 5, pp. 135–140; Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, Lemma 3.4
sources.notes: Primary author proof. Theorem 3.3 states NP ⊆ BPP implies PH ⊆ BPP. Theorem 3.1 gives a randomized formula list preserving unsatisfiability and isolating a solution with high probability.

sources.title: Generalized Lowness and Highness and Probabilistic Complexity Classes
sources.locator: Mathematical Systems Theory 22, pp. 37–46; author-hosted abstract, final sentence
sources.notes: Recovers the Boppana–Håstad–Zachos result coNP ⊆ BP·NP implies PH ⊆ BP·NP. Here BP·NP is AM; it is not the oracle class BPP^NP. The author abstract, not a full-text proof, was rechecked in the September 2026 audit.

sources.title: If NP has polynomial-size circuits, then MA = AM
sources.locator: Theoretical Computer Science 137(2), pp. 279–282; main theorem and publisher abstract
sources.notes: Arvind, Köbler, Schöning, Schuler. DOI 10.1016/0304-3975(95)91133-B. Publisher abstract and author publication list were checked; full publisher PDF was not accessible during this audit.

sources.locator: Elementary implications added during this audit

sources.title: Length-regular padding review
sources.notes: A recorded derivation from historical definitions, independently reviewed by three domain agents. No new historical publication date is asserted.

sources.title: Unconditional Lower Bounds against Advice
sources.notes: For each fixed c, NEXP is not contained in polynomial time with at most n^c NP queries and n^c advice bits. Theta2P uses O(log n) queries and no advice. Do not take a union over c on the right to infer NEXP not in Delta2P.

sources.title: Nondeterministic Circuit Lower Bounds from Mildly Derandomizing Arthur-Merlin Games
sources.notes: The unconditional consequence of PSPACE subset NP/poly is PSPACE subset Sigma3P, hence PH. Its stronger Sigma2P consequence has an additional promise-AM derandomization assumption and is not imported.

sources.inspection_notes: Original revised full paper inspected. The stated FewP special case proves the proposed conditional rule. Its promise-SBP results are not an unconditional SZK inclusion.

The main theorem gives MA = AM if NP has polynomial-size circuits; the reverse inclusion is already in the baseline.

Run an amplified BPP SAT decider while fixing one variable at a time. A union bound makes every adaptive query correct with probability at least 2/3 on satisfiable inputs. Accept only after deterministically checking the final assignment. Unsatisfiable inputs are never accepted, so SAT and then every NP language are in RP. The source provides the historical SAT self-reduction and error-amplification ingredients; this sentence is the audit derivation.

Use the formula list from Theorem 3.1 and a deterministic parity-SAT decider. Accept if any formula has an odd number of solutions. If the input is unsatisfiable, every formula is unsatisfiable and acceptance is impossible. If satisfiable, with high probability some formula has exactly one solution. Thus SAT is in RP. This uses a total parity solver and does not assume that a solver for the total-language class UP solves the Unique-SAT promise problem.

The unconditional collapse is to Sigma3P, a subclass of PH. No promise-AM derandomization is assumed.

Hardwiring gives NP/poly = P/poly under the premise. P/poly is closed under complement and polynomial-size composition; eliminate each fixed finite number of PH quantifier blocks. See research/classical-notes.md.

Theorem1 and its explicit FewP special case give AM=SBP if 3-SAT is in FewP. NP subset FewP supplies that hypothesis. The reverse inclusion SBP subset AM is already known; the UP premise is subsumed by UP subset FewP.

class_recommendations.uniform_nc: NC means logspace-uniform polynomial-size bounded-fan-in circuits of polylogarithmic depth.
class_recommendations.circuit_semantics: AC0, ACC0, TC0 and NC1 are NONUNIFORM families. ACC0 allows a fixed arbitrary modulus m ≥ 2 per family, equivalently a fixed finite set of moduli.
class_recommendations.advice_semantics: Ppoly and NPpoly use arbitrary polynomial-length advice, possibly uncomputable.
class_recommendations.problem_semantics: All classes are sets of total decision languages over binary strings. Randomized/quantum definitions impose a gap for every input. Quantum gate sets must be fixed and computable.
class_recommendations.omitted_class: NISZK omitted from the initial 51; final selection fixed by root.

cutoff_limitations: Historical classification review and its residual uncertainty are recorded in research/baseline-audit.json and the versioned audit dossiers. Absence from the relation closure alone does not certify that a pair was open.
No paper proof in this file is machine-checked. Lean semantics must not turn citations into hidden axioms or declare abstract graph soundness to be a mechanized proof of the cited theorems.

The benchmark-specific elementary derivations, including nonuniform witnesses, space simulations, padding and advice diagonalization, received independent mathematical cross-review in the audit dossiers. Their existing proofs are trusted rather than re-formalized.

Quantitative hardness, fine-grained improvements, promise problems, search/function classes, algebraic classes VP/VNP, and independence metatheorems need richer propositions than ordered language-class pairs.
E ⊄ Ppoly does not by itself justify BPP ⊆ P via IW1997. The required premise is an exponential circuit lower bound with appropriate quantifiers over lengths.
Kannan fixed-degree circuit lower bounds do not establish Sigma2P ⊄ Ppoly. Do not reverse quantifiers over language and polynomial degree.
Toda gives PH ⊆ P^PP, not PH ⊆ PP. A low-level PH collapse does not automatically collapse counting classes.
BPP = P for total languages does not automatically derandomize promise-BPP verifiers; do not infer MA = NP or BQP = P.
No oracle or communication-complexity separation can be imported as an unrelativized language-class separation.
Primary-source publication dates are historical bibliographic dates. Search-engine crawl dates and stale PDF template footers were not used as publication dates.
